findings.description: Permanent-vs-Transient carry-forward asymmetry is entirely code-side surplus. SHEET-MARK-004 says only 'stamp each cached mark with GOOGLEFINANCE's quote date, not wall-clock' — it says nothing about what happens across settle cycles when a symbol degrades. The real code (lib.rs read_marks, lines ~870-884) draws a sharp line: on `PriceReading::Transient`/absent past the bounded window, it carries the PRIOR `Mark` forward unchanged — `out.marks.insert(s.clone(), *prev)`, preserving that mark's old `quote_date` verbatim (test: `transient_keeps_prior_mark_and_retries_degrades_only_after_window`, asserting `Mark{price_cents: Cents(180_00), quote_date: Date(19_100)}` survives). But on `PriceReading::Permanent`, the code discards any prior mark entirely — `out.degraded.insert(s.clone(), DegradeReason::Permanent)`, no carry (test: `permanent_error_degrades_immediately_no_prior_carry`, explicit comment 'NOT carried from prior (it is a terminal error, not a transient)'). All 3 B outputs (B1 #6/#8, B2 #4/#5, B3 #5/#7) independently reconstruct this exact asymmetry with high agreement. None of the 3 A outputs model carry-forward at all — their sketches are single-shot 'readback -> stamp' functions with no notion of a settle-cycle history or a prior-mark input, so this whole mechanism (which governs when a wall-clock-free stamp persists vs. gets wiped) is invisible from the spec-only side.

The exact GOOGLEFINANCE quote-date encoding formula is code-side surplus. Real code (`quote_date_formula`, lib.rs lines 270-274): `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` — truncates raw tradetime to its date serial via INT() (dropping time-of-day), rebases to days-since-1970-01-01 (the kernel `Date` epoch) by subtracting `DATE(1970,1,1)`, renders via `TEXT(...,"0")` as a digits-only locale-invariant string (because raw `tradetime` is locale-formatted and unparseable without locale rules), and falls back to empty string `""` via the outer `IFERROR` while loading/errored. SHEET-MARK-004's text states only the outcome ('stamp with quote date, not wall-clock') — none of the mechanism that actually makes that possible without wall-clock substitution (the 1970 rebasing, the TEXT-as-digits trick, the IFERROR-to-empty-string fallback) appears anywhere in the spec. All 3 B outputs converge on reconstructing this formula near-verbatim (B1 #4/#7, B2 #8, B3 #2/#3) — high stability. This is the strongest, most concrete drift: a hard constant/encoding contract enforced by the code and its formula-construction function, wholly absent from the EARS text.

SubCent degrade discards a genuinely-read (non-wall-clock) quote_date, and this rule is pure code surplus. When a `Numeric` reading's price converts to `Cents <= 0` via `price_to_cents` (e.g., the `0.0001` -> 0 cents boundary, or exact `0.0`/negative), `read_marks` records the symbol degraded (`SubCent`) with NO `Mark` produced at all (lib.rs ~854-868; tests `subcent_positive_price_is_degraded_anomaly_not_zero`, `zero_and_negative_price_are_degraded_not_a_zero_or_negative_mark`) — even though that same pass legitimately read a valid GOOGLEFINANCE `quote_date` (e.g. `Date(19_150)` in the test fixture). The valid, non-wall-clock date is simply thrown away rather than attached to any record. SHEET-MARK-004's text presumes a mark gets produced and stamped; it says nothing about a valid quote-date read being discardable when the paired price fails a downstream, unrelated validation (Cents rounding). B1 #10 and B2 #6 both call this out explicitly and consistently ('the reading's quote_date is discarded, never attached to a fabricated zero mark') — medium-high B agreement (B3 does not spell this out as explicitly as B1/B2, folding it into its more general framing in point 8).

notes: No material A-side (spec-surplus) findings survive: all 3 A outputs invent a concrete quote-date parsing/cell-representation mechanism (chrono NaiveDate + Sheets serial epoch 1899-12-30 in A2/A3, an opaque upstream-parsed Option<NaiveDate> in A1) and a hard-error-on-missing-quote-date policy — but none of this traces to explicit SHEET-MARK-004 text (which only states the stamp-source requirement, not any parsing mechanism or missing-data error semantics). Per the classification rules this is an unanimous-but-ungrounded assumption artifact, not a finding — the 3 A runs agree on the high-level 'never fall back to wall-clock, fail rather than substitute' theme (hence not rating A agreement 'low') but diverge substantially on the concrete parsing mechanism/cell model (hence not 'high'). Also worth noting: in the real code, `PriceReading::Numeric{price_usd, quote_date: Date}` makes `quote_date` non-optional at the sheets-view boundary — the 'missing/unparseable quote date while price is present' scenario that all 3 A sketches build explicit error handling for is structurally unrepresentable in the real crate (that parsing/validation is pushed entirely into `runtime`, outside sheets-view's scope per its own module doc). This reinforces that A's invented error path has no code-side counterpart to be 'missing' against, since real code doesn't leave that door open in the first place — consistent with treating it as an assumption artifact rather than an A-side drift finding. Two secondary B-side observations (poll-overwrite last-reading-wins state machine, `max_polls` default 8, and transport-failure Err-propagation) appear in all 3 B outputs with high agreement but are tangential to SHEET-MARK-004 specifically — they look like they belong to a sibling settle-pass/bounded-window requirement rather than the quote-date-stamping requirement audited here, so I did not count them as primary SHEET-MARK-004 findings.
